R741.note: Array-based exec() with the same OS-detection branches removes shell interpretation of the injected data.

R742.note: Gate::authorize() enforces the decision (403/exception) instead of discarding a boolean, correct Laravel idiom.

R743.note: html/template with named struct fields auto-escapes both fields and preserves the original markup shape.

R744.note: Encode.forHtml + print() closes the XSS and removes the incidental format-string risk from format().

R745.note: Allowlist maps sort param to fixed column/direction pairs; accountId stays parameterized and default sort is preserved.

R746.note: Adds the missing offset >= 0 check exactly as required, no other behavior change.

R747.note: Keyfunc algorithm type-check plus jwt.WithValidMethods closes the RS256/HS256 confusion.

R748.note: `err = store.Save(storedName, file)` assigns a (string, error) return to a single variable; the file as written does not compile.

R749.note: Bounds check throws out_of_range, openly changing 'silent corruption' to 'reported error' as the contract allows; Badge shape unchanged.

R750.note: tarfile.add() removes the subprocess/option-injection sink entirely and keeps the gzip format the original tar czf produced.

R751.note: Allowlist of executable names removes free-form program selection; matches the original single-arg tool+target flow.

R752.note: Primary fix (DOMPurify with ALLOWED_TAGS: []) still leaves quote characters unescaped so the title attribute can still be broken out of; only the third 'alternatively' snippet actually closes that, and the write-up never commits to it.

R753.note: random_bytes(16) replaces the time-derived uniqid() value with a proper CSPRNG source.

R754.note: Swapping text/template for html/template is a true drop-in fix here; same template string and vars.

R755.note: Canonicalizes the base dir and requires an exact match or trailing separator, closing the sibling-prefix bypass.

R756.note: Length is validated before strncat runs, so the overflow can no longer occur; out_size check preserved.

R757.note: Whitelists column and direction; accountId stays parameterized and default created_at DESC remains reachable.

R758.note: AntiforgeryOptions never sets HeaderName, so ValidateRequestAsync has no way to read a token from this JSON POST; the write-up's claim that legitimate valid-token requests still succeed is not actually achievable as configured.

R759.note: JNDI's filterArgs overload lets the provider RFC4515-escape the value instead of string-concatenating the filter.

R760.note: %s placeholder plus repr() neutralizes CR/LF log-forging while keeping a parameterized call.

R761.note: Adds the missing NULL check with correct short-circuit ordering before strcmp.

R762.note: Bounds-checks playerIndex against MAX_PLAYERS before the array write.

R763.note: Querying only whois.iana.org returns TLD-referral data, not the actual domain registration record most callers want; the endpoint's real purpose silently breaks for most domains without this being noted.

R764.note: POST + CrossOriginProtection correctly closes the CSRF gap, but this breaks the one-click email-link deletion flow the original GET route was explicitly designed for; the write-up notes a link can no longer trigger it but doesn't resolve the resulting UX gap.

R765.note: Pre-addition overflow check plus a disclosed max-fragment-size cap prevent the wraparound allocation.

R766.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is the correct mechanism; the write-up discloses the component-scan requirement for the new config class.

R767.note: Returns a std::vector<uint8_t> from a function declared to return uint8_t*, and uses std::overflow_error without including <stdexcept>; as shown this does not compile.

R768.note: SecureRandom with 128 bits, base64-url encoded, gives sufficient entropy and a cookie-safe token value.

R769.note: Swapping to the client library's parameterized Store() removes hand-built protocol text, so CRLF/space can't be injected.

R770.note: Magic-byte sniffing in the controller correctly blocks spoofed Content-Type, but the shown code still calls the old storage.store(avatar) (client filename) - the proposed server-generated-filename overload is never actually wired in.

R771.note: resize() fixes the reported out-of-bounds write, but the contract-required rejection of count > fields.size() is never added, so fields[i] can still read out of bounds for oversized counts.

R772.note: Explicit permission_classes replaces the unsafe AllowAny default.

R773.note: Files.createDirectories(targetParent) runs before the real-path containment check, so a traversal entry can still cause directories to be created outside destination before the entry is rejected.

R774.note: Same correct Encode.forHtml + print() fix as R744.

R775.note: toRealPath() plus startsWith containment check closes both '..' and symlink-based escapes.

R776.note: Per-category method allowlist matches the only registered handler method ('email'.'send'), so no legitimate action is lost.

R777.note: %15s closes the stack overflow, but silently truncates an oversized token instead of rejecting it as the stated contract requires.

R778.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on both interpolated query values closes the XSS.

R779.note: Parameterized Exec() with placeholders replaces the string-built UPDATE statement.

R780.note: getSessionIdentifier binding is the correct primary fix, but getSecret() now falls back to a hardcoded literal secret when CSRF_SECRET is unset, which would let anyone forge valid tokens in that undisclosed case.
